description:
Germany's River Rhine has fallen to historically low water levels as severe drought disrupts inland shipping and puts further pressure on the country's economy and supply chains.

The Rhine is a vital transport route for fuel, grain and other essential goods. With ships unable to carry normal loads, businesses face higher transportation costs and growing disruption.

The drought is also devastating Germany's agricultural sector, with farmers reporting some of their worst grain harvests on record. The combination of reduced crop yields and rising transport costs could push food prices higher for consumers.

Correspondent Rebecca Collard reports from Germany on the impact of the drought, the pressure on farmers and the wider economic consequences of Europe's changing climate.

description:
Puerto Rico is desperate for water again. Extreme drought has forced the government to ration water on a rotating 48-hour schedule, affecting more than 180,000 people. San Juan has recorded its driest July in over 120 years, and reservoir levels are running critically low. Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez has activated the National Guard to help distribute water after a major line was damaged, though she says she doesn't know when the rationing will end. It's the third time in about a decade the U.S. territory has had to ration water, with recovery from past hurricanes and delayed federal infrastructure funding compounding the crisis. On an island where 40% of the population lives in poverty, access to water is becoming increasingly scarce. 

Al Jazeera's Matthew Torres reports from San Juan.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
More than 300 people kidnapped from their communities in February have been rescued by the Nigerian military after weeks of operation. 
Many of them are in terrible conditions, having spent more than six months in captivity. 
This is the first time they are breathing the air of freedom. 
When gunmen attacked their community, they killed more than 150 people, burned down the entire village, and destroyed their means of livelihood. 
Many of the rescued will be returning to almost nothing, finding their homes, farms, and businesses completely destroyed. 
Among the rescued are tired and sick children, women, and men. 
They are currently being housed in a hotel—their first decent accommodation in six months—before being moved to a medical facility for health review. 
The military coordinated the formal handover of the released captives to civilian authorities in Kwara State. 

Al Jazeera's Ahmed Idris reports from Ilorin, central Nigeria.

title: More than 300 captives freed in Nigerian military rescue operation

description:
South Korea's Kospi index has swung wildly this year, more than doubling to pass 9,000 points before crashing 40 percent, triggering automatic trading suspensions over 50 times. Analysts point to a combination of government intervention, deregulation of exchange-traded funds and heavy reliance on AI chipmakers Samsung and SK Hynix, which now account for over half the market. Small investors, including teenagers borrowing to buy shares, say they are bearing the brunt of the volatility, fuelling public anger and calls for the government to step back.

Al Jazeera’s Jack Barton reports from Seoul, South Korea.

The World Health Organization says it has received less than half the funding needed for an effective response, as the outbreak spreads across five provinces. Nearly 4,000 people have been infected and more than 1,800 have died. Officials blame logistical challenges for the payment delays, while the UN warns disruptions could hinder efforts to break transmission chains.

Al Jazeera’s Felix Nyawara reports from Bunia, Democratic Republic of Congo.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In Argentina, police have clashed with protesters opposing a controversial property reform bill, with security forces using water cannons and tear gas on demonstrators in Buenos Aires. The legislation aims to strengthen private property rights, but a provision easing restrictions on foreign purchases of rural land was removed after widespread backlash. Indigenous groups warn the reforms could weaken protections for ancestral lands. Thousands gathered outside Congress as the Senate debated the bill, chanting "Argentina is not for sale." The government says the law is needed to attract foreign investment, while critics argue it could put Argentina's land and natural resources at risk. Existing rules allow foreigners to own around 15 percent of Argentina's territory, and opponents say that limit should not be expanded. Protesters say they will remain on the streets after forcing the government to remove a key part of the legislation. 

Al Jazeera's Teresa Bo reports from Buenos Aires.

title: Argentina police clash with protesters over controversial property reform bill

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
In an interview with Al Jazeera, University of Chicago professor Robert Pape warned that the United States is caught in what he called "the most wicked escalation trap in history" with Iran. 
He said US air and naval strikes have achieved tactical successes but have "failed to achieve any of its strategic objectives," arguing that Iran has emerged stronger than before the war. 
Pape said President Donald Trump faces a choice between accepting Iran's growing influence or escalating the conflict further, saying: "There's no third option." 
He warned that Trump is already seeing the limits of air and naval power and could be pushed towards ground operations, potentially seeking a symbolic victory ahead of the midterm elections. 
Pape also argued that Trump would struggle to accept Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz and predicted continued escalation. 
He warned that Iran could move towards testing nuclear weapons within two to three years if the current trajectory continues.

Subs
title: Trump is caught in an "escalation trap" in Iran war: Analysis

description: Explosions were reported on Iran's southern Qeshm Island, with Iranian state media saying operations targeted what it described as hostile targets. The incident comes as tensions remain high around the Strait of Hormuz following a brief period of de-escalation between Iran and the United States. Iran's parliament is discussing a draft bill to tighten Tehran's control over the strategic waterway, including restrictions and possible fines targeting vessels from the US, Israel and other countries it considers hostile. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump says he believes the war with Iran could end soon, arguing Washington's military action was necessary to prevent Tehran from developing a nuclear weapon. Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused the US of "theater diplomacy", saying Washington was switching between military threats and calls for negotiations. The developments come as Iran and Oman work on a temporary agreement to allow commercial vessels to pass through
title: Explosions reported in Iran’s Qeshm Island amid tensions over Hormuz Strait

description:
Yemen's Ansar Allah group, commonly referred to as the Houthis, say they killed 45 people in attacks on Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces in the east of the country, using ballistic missiles and drones to target military positions in Hadramout and Marib provinces.
 The strikes targeted the al-Thiniya camp and other areas, with government forces confirming casualties from the attacks. 
The escalation marks a shift in Houthi operations, which had previously focused on Israeli-linked shipping and regional infrastructure. 
The group says it is targeting forces it accuses of working with Saudi Arabia against its control of Yemen. In a separate incident, Saudi Arabia's military coalition says 11 civilians were wounded in a Houthi attack on the southern border region of Najran, including seven Saudi nationals, a woman and a child. 
The Houthis say they targeted Najran airport as part of their campaign against Saudi Arabia in response to earlier Saudi strikes on Sanaa International Airpor
title: Houthis claim 45 killed in attacks on Yemen government forces; Saudi Arabia reports Najran strike
